clue.text: Realistic stage of an astronaut's journey

definitions.meaning: a practical, sensible person with no fanciful ideas is described with this phrase
the last leg of a space flight is the return descent back to our planet

explanation.definitionFit: Being sensible and unpretentious is an idiom for having one's feet on the ground; the literal reading is the descent home from orbit.

clue.text: Misgiving about the French garment

indicators.note: the word for misgiving goes around the French article, enclosing it

parts.note: a misgiving is a doubt
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone has qualms about a French item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts LE inside DOUBT, giving DOUB-LE-T.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting jacket worn by men from the 14th to 17th centuries is a type of garment.

clue.text: Bird gets the boot

definitions.meaning: a long-legged bird such as a heron that feeds in shallow water
a high waterproof boot worn by anglers

explanation.definitionFit: A heron or stork wades in the shallows, and an angler's thigh-high rubber boot shares that name.

clue.text: Peruse article about stringing beads

indicators.note: the word for article wraps around the word for peruse

parts.note: an article is an object, a thing
to peruse is to read

explanation.surface: A reader studies a magazine article about bead jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts READ inside THING: TH-READ-ING. 'article' means an object, not a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringing beads means passing a cord or thread through each one.

clue.text: Girl has the right at all times

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A girl is always in the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever, as in 'ever ready', means always, constantly.

clue.text: Again capturing king in great exchange

indicators.note: the letters are swapped around among themselves into a new order

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A chess player retakes the king during a big swap of pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange' rearranges K (king) with IN and GREAT to give RETAKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking back something lost means seizing it once more.

clue.text: A five in an awful hole, a miserable dwelling

indicators.note: the Roman numeral sits inside the scrambled letters
something awful is a mess, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A handful of people crammed into a dreadful hole, a wretched place to live.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper text reads 'few' where the wordplay needs 'five'. 'awful' scrambles HOLE to HOEL, and 'in' puts V inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hovel is a squalid, poorly built hut or shack.

clue.text: Instance was more than enough

parts.note: ex means former, something that was
ample means plentiful, more than sufficient

explanation.surface: One occasion was more than plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was' gives EX, as in an ex-husband: one who was a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a case or specimen illustrating a type.

clue.text: Toy brick takes a long time to cause an obstruction

parts.note: a child's wooden building brick is a block
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A toy brick takes ages to clog something up.
explanation.definitionFit: A clogged pipe or road contains a stoppage that prevents flow.

clue.text: Not above having examined what is next to the floorboards

definitions.text: what is next to the floorboards

parts.note: below or beneath is the opposite of above
felt means touched to examine, as a doctor feels a lump

explanation.surface: Someone is not too proud to inspect what lies under the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not above' sounds like 'not too proud to', but it gives UNDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Underfelt is the felt padding laid beneath a carpet, directly on the floorboards.

clue.text: Home I will have in Virginia

indicators.note: the contraction goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Someone plans to have a house in Virginia.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a large country or holiday house, a residence.

clue.text: Trail a sort of noose

indicators.note: to sort letters is to rearrange them, so this phrase signals a jumble

explanation.surface: A cowboy follows a trail with a looped rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges TRAIL plus A into LARIAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a lasso, a rope with a running loop for catching cattle.

clue.text: Plant on the top of one's head

definitions.meaning: a flowering herb of the mint family with a helmet-shaped flower

definitions.text: on the top of one's head
definitions.meaning: a small close-fitting brimless cap worn on the crown

explanation.definitionFit: The herb Scutellaria is named for its hood-shaped flowers, and the same name is given to a small cap worn on the crown.

clue.text: Go round with very little money for a vegetable

annotationWithheld.why: Go round with very little money for a vegetable (6): TURN (go round) + P (very little money) gives only TURNP; no clue word supplies the I of TURNIP, and no source for the clue was found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Go round with very little money for a vegetable

clue.text: Having a hard time with indigestible food

parts.note: rough means harsh or hard, as in a rough time
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone has a tough time digesting a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughage is dietary fibre, plant matter the gut cannot break down.

clue.text: I meant it to become very personal

indicators.note: the letters are made to turn into something new, a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A speaker insists a remark was meant to be deeply private.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become' rearranges I MEANT IT into INTIMATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimate matters are private and closely personal.

clue.text: In fun laze about despite suffering from this

definitions.text: In fun laze about despite suffering from this

indicators.note: about means scattered around, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A patient lolls about cheerfully despite being laid low by a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges IN FUN LAZE into INFLUENZA; the whole clue also describes the illness, which keeps a sufferer lazing in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Flu is a viral illness that leaves a patient bedridden and listless.

clue.text: With about half the clues the players were dejected

parts.note: in a crossword roughly half the clues are the downs, the others being acrosses
the cast is the set of actors in a show

explanation.surface: Having solved only half the clues, the team was gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: A crossword's clues split into acrosses and downs, so roughly half are DOWN clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Downcast means low in spirits, depressed.

clue.text: The way to encourage fish

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
to urge on is to spur or encourage

explanation.surface: Advice on the best way to egg someone on.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large fish whose roe is caviar.

clue.text: Scout leader, one who is intent to run

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: read as 'in tent', someone sleeping under canvas

explanation.surface: A Scout leader, focused and determined, sets off at a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intent' splits as 'in tent': a person in a tent is a CAMPER.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to dash or scurry about quickly.

clue.text: Hurt the feeling of one side before the finish

indicators.note: the first piece comes ahead of the second in the answer

parts.note: in cricket the off side is one half of the field
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: Someone hurts another's feelings just before things wrap up.
explanation.walkthrough: The OFF side is one half of a cricket field.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend is to upset or insult someone.

clue.text: Undesirable quality of continental order

parts.note: de is the French for 'of'
the Order of Merit is a British order of honour

explanation.surface: A fault found in some European order of chivalry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'continental' signals a European language: French de means 'of'. MERIT stands for the Order of Merit.
explanation.definitionFit: A demerit is a fault or a mark against someone.

clue.text: He daren't upset one of his followers

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into disorder

explanation.surface: A leader is afraid to annoy one of his disciples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges HE DARENT into ADHERENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a supporter or disciple of a cause or leader.

clue.text: Get up about noon and wash

indicators.note: the word for getting up goes around the letter for noon

parts.note: to rise is to get up

explanation.surface: Someone gets out of bed around midday and has a wash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N inside RISE: RI-N-SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse is to wash lightly in clean water.

clue.text: Singular duty makes copper most upset

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A single tax payment greatly annoys a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges MOST into STOM. 'Singular' is there because the duties paid at a border are 'customs', plural.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom is a tax on imports, usually named in the plural.

clue.text: Levy the object inside

indicators.note: the pronoun is placed within the word printed as 'the'

parts.note: taken as written
it is the pronoun for an object, a thing

explanation.surface: A tax on whatever object lies within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts IT within THE: T-IT-HE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a tenth of produce paid as a tax to the church.

clue.text: Obscenity must be destroyed

indicators.note: something destroyed is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Indecent material must be wiped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be destroyed' rearranges MUST into SMUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is lewd or pornographic material.

clue.text: It is not Christian finding silver in a shallow vessel

indicators.note: the metal symbol sits within the vessel

parts.note: a pan is a shallow container
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Unchristian behaviour: finding silver in a pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts AG inside PAN: P-AG-AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagan is a heathen, a follower of a non-Christian religion.

clue.text: A cross I leave clergyman in Devon

parts.note: taken as written
X is a cross shape

indicators.note: one letter must depart from the word for the clergyman

parts.note: a minister is a member of the clergy

explanation.surface: A cross clergyman storms off, angry, somewhere in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I leave' removes one I from MINISTER, giving MINSTER. Devon is a county in south-west England; AXMINSTER is a town there, famous for carpets.
explanation.definitionFit: Axminster is a market town located in the county of Devon, England.

clue.text: One whose role is that of an accommodating go-between

definitions.text: One whose role is that of an accommodating go-between

parts.words: One whose role is that of an accommodating go-between
parts.note: accommodating means finding accommodation: a middleman who brokers house sales between buyers and sellers

explanation.definitionFit: A property dealer acts as intermediary between people selling and buying homes.
